records.description: A clean https URL on a retailer's own bare apex domain is a safe URL and resolves to a known retailer identity.
records.notes: safe:true is grounded in isSafeCommerceUrl (services/commerceDestination.ts:56-69), SOURCE-SHAPE: https protocol, no embedded username/password, non-private hostname. isAggregator:false is grounded in isAggregatorDestination/AGGREGATOR_HOSTS (services/commerceDestination.ts:21-24,40-49), SOURCE-SHAPE: zappos.com is not in that fixed 8-host list. 'retailerIdentity: known' / 'retailerName' is illustrative/SYNTHETIC: no repo-internal retailer registry exists to classify a domain as a known retailer (Commerce V2 owns building the real one).

records.description: www, regional, and marketplace subdomains of the same retailer all resolve to the same retailer identity and are all safe; per Section 16 these subdomain variants must not be conflated with 'unknown retailer' just because the hostname isn't the bare apex domain.
records.notes: safe:true / isAggregator:false for all three entries is grounded in isSafeCommerceUrl and isAggregatorDestination (services/commerceDestination.ts:21-24,40-69), SOURCE-SHAPE: none of these checks look at subdomain structure at all, so www./uk./marketplace. pass identically to the bare apex. 'retailerIdentity: known' / matching all three to the same retailer name is illustrative/SYNTHETIC: no repo-internal retailer registry or subdomain-normalization rule exists yet (Commerce V2 owns building one).

records.description: A third-party affiliate-redirect-shaped domain is a safe https URL (no embedded credentials, not a private host) but is not a direct retailer identity -- retailer identity stays unknown/unresolved from the URL alone, unlike dom-exact-merchant-domain.
records.notes: safe:true is grounded in isSafeCommerceUrl (services/commerceDestination.ts:56-69), SOURCE-SHAPE. isAggregator:false is grounded in isAggregatorDestination checking only the fixed 8-host AGGREGATOR_HOSTS list (services/commerceDestination.ts:21-24,40-49) -- this redirect domain is not on that list, SOURCE-SHAPE. Whether a domain is a genuine retailer vs. a generic affiliate-redirect middleman is illustrative/SYNTHETIC: no repo-internal registry distinguishes them, so today's real code would treat this host the same as any other non-aggregator safe URL -- a gap worth flagging for Commerce V2, not a bug being asserted here.

records.description: A generic shared redirect host and a generic shared CDN/image host, both used by many unrelated retailers, cannot establish retailer identity from the hostname alone -- both remain safe URLs but resolve to unknown-retailer.
records.notes: safe:true / isAggregator:false for both entries is grounded in isSafeCommerceUrl and isAggregatorDestination (services/commerceDestination.ts:21-24,40-69), SOURCE-SHAPE. The 'a shared host cannot establish identity' classification is illustrative/SYNTHETIC: no repo-internal registry of shared redirect/CDN hosts vs. retailer-owned hosts exists (Commerce V2 owns building one).

records.description: A domain with no recognizable retailer signal at all is still a safe https URL but resolves to no known retailer identity.
records.notes: safe:true is grounded in isSafeCommerceUrl (services/commerceDestination.ts:56-69) and isAggregator:false in isAggregatorDestination (services/commerceDestination.ts:21-24,40-49), both SOURCE-SHAPE. 'unknown-retailer' itself is illustrative/SYNTHETIC since no repo-internal retailer registry exists yet (Commerce V2 owns building one).

records.description: A string that does not parse as a URL at all is rejected outright and never reaches retailer classification.
records.notes: isSafeCommerceUrl (services/commerceDestination.ts:56-69) wraps `new URL(text)` in try/catch and returns null on a parse failure -- exactly the 'not a url {{' case.

records.description: An otherwise well-formed retailer URL is rejected solely because its scheme is http, not https -- contrast with dom-exact-merchant-domain, the identical host over https, which passes.
records.notes: isSafeCommerceUrl (services/commerceDestination.ts:56-69) requires `parsed.protocol !== 'https:' -> null`; http is rejected regardless of how legitimate the host looks.

records.description: A URL carrying embedded username:password-style credentials is rejected outright, regardless of protocol or host.
records.notes: isSafeCommerceUrl (services/commerceDestination.ts:56-69) rejects any URL where `parsed.username || parsed.password` is truthy. Placeholder-only credentials ('fake-user'/'fake-pass') on a .test domain -- not a real credential shape.

records.description: A legitimate retailer https URL carrying a long signed-looking query string plus ordinary utm_ tracking parameters is still safe: isSafeCommerceUrl only inspects protocol, embedded username/password, and hostname, and never rejects on query-string content -- contrast with dom-credential-shaped-url, where basic-auth-style user:pass@ credentials embedded IN the URL (a different, rejected risk class) cause rejection.
records.notes: isSafeCommerceUrl (services/commerceDestination.ts:56-69) never reads `parsed.search` at all -- SOURCE-SHAPE for the safe:true determination, which is unaffected by the utm_/sig/expires query params. 'retailerIdentity: known' is illustrative/SYNTHETIC since no repo-internal registry exists yet; included only to show hostname resolution is unaffected by the query string. Note: this module (commerceDestination.ts) is distinct from services/dressingRoomCommerce.ts's normalizePersistedCommerceUrl, which DOES reject 'sig'/'expires' query keys for persisted purchase-option/image URLs (see products/product-image.json#img-signed-credential-shaped) -- the two safety checks are not the same function and do not agree on this exact query shape.
